svg.text: 2 • Local AI Flow — Who Calls Which Model, and What Falls Back to What
OpenAI-compatible local inference on Apple Silicon, Ollama on two machines, and two SEPARATE Hermes installs with different primaries
All requests start as tasks, not raw GPUs
• Box: NO GPU, 15 GB shared RAM
• → Never run local models on Box
• → Box must CALL OUT to Mini /
Why a proxy? No kernel TUN on shared VM
MLX on Apple Silicon • unified memory
• 1× 9B at a time • max 2 concurrent • ~6 s cold load
• Not exposed on tailnet — SSH in first
• qwen3:8b / qwen3.5:9b — local coding assist + sweeps
• gemma4:e4b — no assigned job yet (EXP-005 to prove)
• Ollama: qwen3:8b — bulk local coding assist
• 62 GB RAM = larger context / heavy builds
• Access via Grok Bot machine access —
• not a documented Box Ollama path
• ⚠ gfx1032 is older ROCm tier — check
• No cron / no gateway on Box Hermes
• ⚠ oMLX is NOT a login item:
~6 s cold load = first token waits for
weights into unified memory. Warm ≠ free.
fails — design bots for back-off, not fan-out.
That is how 9B fits an 11.3 GiB budget —
with quality loss that is task-dependent.
Larger models still may not fit usefully.
bge-m3 turns text → vectors for search /
RAG. It is not a chat model.
Do not benchmark chat tok/s on either.
oMLX speaks the OpenAI /v1 shape locally,
so tools swap base-URL, not code.
a local 9B ≠ a frontier cloud model.
That gap is exactly why Hermes keeps
Box → Omarchy: UNVERIFIED — path/ACL not documented
⚠ KNOWN UNVERIFIED — Verified 2026-10-17; items below were NOT live-checked in this audit
Tailnet ACL details (no ACL file check) • Omarchy specs (Ian/Atlas-verified only)

Sources: wiki content/infra/local-ai.md, box.md, macs.md, omarchy.md • Model names/speeds as documented Oct 2026 • No API keys, tailnet IPs, or key-file contents shown • Verified 2026-10-17 (oMLX via SOCKS5) • UNVERIFIED = marked, not assumed
Box Hermes: cloud gpt-6.1-sol FIRST, DeepSeek/MiniMax if it fails. Local oMLX is not in its chain at all.
Mini Hermes: MiniMax-M3 FIRST, oMLX only if cloud fails. Cron therefore depends on cloud + a manually-started local server.
Bots do not pick GPUs directly — they ask Hermes / an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and routing decides where tokens come from.
